plan: In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of what other bidders do. This is because if I win, I pay the second-highest bid (not my own bid), so bidding higher than my value risks winning and overpaying (paying more than the item's worth to me), while bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. Since my value is $10, I should bid exactly $10 to maximize expected profit, letting the second-price mechanism work in my favor.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of what others do, since you pay the second-highest bid, not your own bid. Overbidding risks paying more than the item is worth to you, while underbidding risks losing profitable auctions. Therefore, the optimal strategy is straightforward: bid exactly my true value of $30.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction (Vickrey auction). In such auctions, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of what other bidders do - it doesn't matter if they bid truthfully, aggressively, or conservatively. Since I pay the second-highest bid if I win, bidding exactly my value ensures I win whenever it's profitable (value > second-highest bid) and lose when it's not profitable, without any risk of overpaying. My value is $25, so I will bid $25.
